nodes.description: mapping(address => uint256) public balances: ETH deposited per account, later converted to token entitlements.
bool public bought_tokens: gate flag controlling whether the presale buy-in has happened.
uint256 public contract_eth_value: ETH value of tokens held by the contract, used as the withdrawal denominator.
uint256 public eth_cap = 500 ether: maximum ETH the contract will accept.
uint256 constant public min_required_amount = 60 ether: minimum balance needed before the buy-in.
address public owner: privileged account allowed to buy tokens and raise the cap.
address public sale: hard-coded presale wallet that receives the pooled ETH.
Constructor: sets owner = msg.sender.
perform_withdrawal(address tokenAddress): lets a depositor withdraw a proportional share of ERC20 tokens after the buy-in.
refund_me(): lets any caller withdraw his recorded ETH balance.
buy_the_tokens(): owner-only function that forwards the pooled ETH to the presale address via a low-level call.
upgrade_cap(): owner-only function that raises eth_cap to 1000 ether.
function () payable: default deposit entry point that credits balances[msg.sender] with msg.value.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership, balance accounting and payout recipients.
External call token.transfer(msg.sender, tokens_to_withdraw) on an attacker-supplied ERC20 address.
External ETH send msg.sender.transfer(eth_to_withdraw) in refund_me.
Low-level call sale.call.value(contract_eth_value)() forwarding all pooled ETH.
Arithmetic state update contract_eth_value -= balances[msg.sender] in perform_withdrawal.
Arithmetic deposit accounting balances[msg.sender] += msg.value in the payable fallback.
User-supplied ERC20 token address passed to perform_withdrawal.
Local ERC20 instance cast from tokenAddress.
Cached token.balanceOf(address(this)) used as the pro-rata numerator.
Computed token payout: balances[msg.sender] * contract_token_balance / contract_eth_value.
Snapshot of balances[msg.sender] taken before it is zeroed in refund_me.

edges.reason: msg.sender is stored as owner during construction.
Constructor writes the owner state variable.
msg.sender indexes balances in perform_withdrawal.
msg.sender indexes balances in refund_me.
msg.sender is compared against owner in buy_the_tokens.
msg.sender is compared against owner in upgrade_cap.
msg.sender keys the deposit accounting in the fallback.
msg.sender is the recipient of token.transfer.
msg.sender is the ETH transfer recipient in refund_me.
tokenAddress is cast into the local ERC20 instance token.
token.transfer is invoked on the user-controlled token instance.
contract_token_balance is the numerator of the pro-rata computation.
balances[msg.sender] is multiplied to compute tokens_to_withdraw.
contract_eth_value is the denominator of the token computation.
Computed tokens_to_withdraw is passed to token.transfer.
balances[msg.sender] is subtracted from contract_eth_value.
contract_eth_value is decremented without a solvency guard on the subtraction path.
perform_withdrawal mutates contract_eth_value.
perform_withdrawal zeroes balances[msg.sender] before the external call.
balances[msg.sender] is copied into eth_to_withdraw.
eth_to_withdraw is the amount sent to msg.sender.
refund_me zeroes balances[msg.sender] before sending ETH.
contract_eth_value is the value forwarded in sale.call.value.
buy_the_tokens sets bought_tokens = true.
buy_the_tokens records the contract balance as contract_eth_value.
upgrade_cap writes eth_cap = 1000 ether.
Fallback executes the deposit accounting statement.
msg.sender keys the balances[msg.sender] += msg.value update.
Unsigned addition credited to balances inside the payable fallback.
require(bought_tokens) gates perform_withdrawal.
require(!bought_tokens) gates the buy-in.
require(!bought_tokens) gates deposits in the fallback.
require(msg.sender == owner) restricts buy_the_tokens to the owner.
require(msg.sender == owner) restricts upgrade_cap to the owner.
eth_cap bounds this.balance + msg.value in the fallback deposit check.
min_required_amount gates the buy-in.
sale is the target address of the low-level value call.
tokenAddress is arbitrary and its transfer callback can re-enter perform_withdrawal.
Sending ETH to msg.sender gives the receiver control that could re-enter refund_me.
The ETH recipient can re-enter the payable fallback and re-credit its balance.
The low-level call to sale re-enters the contract and can re-execute the buy-in path.

normalization_plan.reason: The user-supplied token address parameter only exists to parameterize the perform_withdrawal logic and has no independent semantics.
The local ERC20 instance is only materialized to invoke the token.transfer unsafe operation.
The cached token balance is a transient value used solely within perform_withdrawal.
The computed payout is a scratch value whose only purpose is to be passed to token.transfer.
The ETH snapshot is a transient value consumed exclusively by the msg.sender.transfer unsafe operation.
